messages:
lane-corp-admin: Hey team — we rotated our IdP signing cert at 03:02 UTC and now users get blocked from SSO. Starts with 'Invalid SAML signature' on every login. Nothing else changed on our side.

maya: Ack, sorry about that. Can you paste the exact error you see in the browser or on your side? Screenshots fine. Also, which IdP (Okta/ADFS/Keycloak)?

lane-corp-admin: Okta. Browser error: 'SAML authentication failed: signature verification failed'. From our side the SAMLRequest looks normal. We attached the new metadata XML to the Okta app but still failing.

alex: @lane-corp-admin thanks — can you dump the raw SAMLResponse (base64) or at least the Issuer and Signature element? if not, give us the metadata URL you uploaded.

lane-corp-admin: metadata posted at https://lane-idp.corp/metadata.xml — attaching small excerpt showing KeyDescriptor for signing (we replaced cert).

lane-corp-admin (paste): ```xml
<KeyDescriptor use=\"signing\">
  <KeyInfo>
    <X509Data>
      <X509Certificate>MIIC...newcert...Q==</X509Certificate>
    </X509Data>
  </KeyInfo>
</KeyDescriptor>
```

maya: Good. Quick check from our side: our auth-proxy logs show "signature validation failed: no matching cert found for signature" at 1820000127. That means our cached metadata doesn't have the new cert yet. We periodically fetch metadata every 6h. Did you change the cert within the last hour?

lane-corp-admin: yes rotated ~03:02 UTC (minutes before posting). thought metadata publishing would be immediate.

paul: Two things we see commonly: 1) IdP publishes multiple certificates and the SAML assertion used a cert that isn't first in the KeyDescriptor list, or 2) fingerprint/hash algorithm mismatch — Okta sometimes publishes SHA1 thumbnail and some parsers prefer SHA256. In your metadata I see two KeyDescriptor entries, the new cert is present but under an extra KeyDescriptor with use=\"encryption\" as well as signing in the metadata timeline. Can you confirm there's exactly one signing KeyDescriptor with the new cert?

lane-corp-admin: Huh — Okta UI auto-added an encryption key when we uploaded. I removed the duplicate and re-saved. Still failing.

alex: @paul, can we force the metadata refresh for this tenant? I can’t wait 6h.

paul: Yes. There's an internal endpoint to refresh tenant metadata immediately. Ops-only: `POST /internal/idp/tenants/lane-corp/refresh-metadata` (auth required). I triggered it at 1820000131. Also did a `kubectl rollout restart deploy/redwood-auth-proxy -n redwood` to clear in-memory cache.

sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-2257 assigned to eng-infra, priority P2 — source: support thread 1820000123 :eyes:

maya: After the refresh + restart we see a new GET to your metadata URL and subsequent validation attempts. Can you try logging in now and paste the new SAMLResponse if it still fails?

lane-corp-admin: Tried — success! Users can sign in again. Thanks all.

paul: Root cause summary: Okta upload created a second KeyDescriptor entry and Okta signed assertions with the new cert while our cached metadata still had the old cert ordering. Our parser previously matched certs by certificate content and allowed SHA1-based thumbprints only; in this case Okta exposed SHA256 only. Fixes we applied: immediate metadata refresh endpoint (ops), auth-proxy restart automation when tenant metadata changes, and parser update to accept SHA1/SHA256 thumbprint fields and compare full certificate values.

maya: Follow-ups: 1) ops will document forced refresh flow in support playbook, 2) eng will add a small monitoring check to detect when metadata cert thumbprint changes vs cached value, 3) CS will notify LaneCorp to test rotation in staging and to prefer replacing signing cert in the same KeyDescriptor when possible.

lane-corp-admin: Appreciate the quick turn. Please add me to the postmortem thread for the follow-ups.

maya: Added you, closing this thread once postmortem link is posted. :white_check_mark:
